record.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — before_validation strips scheme and path, so an admin entering `example.com/blog` silently whitelists the entire domain for embedding

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbeddableHost` intentionally normalizes input in `before_validation` by stripping scheme and any path (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), and the model spec explicitly tests that `'https://example.com/1234/45'` becomes `'example.com'`. So the finding (entering `example.com/blog` results in whitelisting the whole domain) is accurate, but it reflects a design/UX/configuration concern rather than an unintended defect in this PR. If path-level allowlisting is not supported, the code/UI should reject or clearly communicate that only hostnames are used instead of silently broadening the scope.
